rationale: The standard requires students to make use of texts for any one of four purposes (build knowledge, develop skills, make informed decisions, share information and ideas) — an OR list per the overlay. Students use the informational text Does the Sun Sleep? to build knowledge about star patterns. Throughout Work Time A, students actively extract information from the text and illustrations: "What is one piece of new information you have learned about patterns of the stars?" with student responses such as "Stars shine only at night; starlight is not as bright as sunlight." Students also answer text-dependent questions demonstrating knowledge-building, e.g., "Why can't we see stars during the day?" ("because the sunlight outshines the starlight; stars are far away so their light is very dim"). The student is the one articulating the knowledge gained from the text, satisfying the actor gate and the build-knowledge purpose.
